title: Talking Point: Xbox Disc To Digital Has Changed How I Buy Games
summary:
I'm buying on Xbox what I'd usually pick up on Steam and other consoles.

Since Xbox announced that physical disc-based games could be converted into digital licenses playable on both console and PC, I've been all-in on physical purchases.

I've always been an advocate for physical ownership, long before disc to digital, but the ability to buy a physical copy of a game and essentially turn it into a PC license - I'm even more so. Xbox's disc to digital programme has got to be one of this console generation's defining features, giving players a genuine reason to reach for games off the shelf, dust 'em off, pop them into the disc tray, and claim digital licenses in the process.

event_model_payload.headline: These Are The Top 10 Xbox Backwards Compatibility Requests After 900,000 Votes
event_model_payload.summary:
Even including PC requests now!

At various times throughout this year, we've had a look at the top 10 Xbox backwards compatibility requests (after 350,000 and 750,000 votes) based on the unofficial Xbox Game Preservation website, which is a source that we know the Xbox team have paid attention to in the past.

Now that we're getting close to the end of the year, there are over 900,000 votes on the website for new backwards compatible titles, and there are also new categories based on things like indie games.
